items.h: Questionable for Week 8
items.s: Skowronek (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports. Skowronek strung together three consecutive limited practices while working through a calf injury, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Steelers' last two games. His status for Sunday's AFC North may become more clear depending on whether the Steelers elect to elevate Brandon Johnson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

items.h: Ben Skowronek (calf) listed questionable for Sunday
items.s: Ben Skowronek (calf) is listed questionable for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns. The veteran wideout will have a chance to play on Sunday. His calf injury has left him sidelined for a little while, but he seems to be close to full health at this point. He won't be fantasy relevant moving forward, however, even if he's cleared to make his return to the lineup on Sunday.

items.h: Logs another limited practice
items.s: Skowronek (calf) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports. Skowronek has missed each of Pittsburgh's past two games due to the calf issue. His ability to begin Week 8 prep with consecutive limited sessions gives the veteran wideout a chance to return Sunday versus Cleveland, though he'll likely carry a designation into the weekend if he's not able to log a full session Friday. When healthy this season, Skowronek has seen limited opportunities on offense, recording just three catches for 32 yards and a touchdown on four targets through five contests.

items.h: Ben Skowronek (calf) limited participant Thursday
items.s: Ben Skowronek (calf) was a limited participant in practice on Thursday. Skowronek was limited for another practice session on Thursday. That's a step in the right direction for him, however, as he has missed multiple games due to the calf injury that's bothering him. He remains off of the injury report moving forward, regardless of his health status.

items.h: Ben Skowronek (calf) limited in practice Wednesday
items.s: Ben Skowronek was limited in practice on Wednesday. Skowronek remains off the fantasy radar.

items.h: Limited at practice Wednesday
items.s: Skowronek (calf) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday. Skowronek has missed the Steelers' last two games with a calf injury he sustained back in Week 5 versus the Colts, and now his availability for Week 8 is up in the air. Whether he ends up suiting up Sunday versus the Browns might hinge on whether he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday.

items.h: Ruled out Week 7
items.s: The Steelers have ruled Skowronek (calf) out for Sunday's matchup against the Saints, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports. Skowronek did not participate in Wednesday's practice. He will now miss his second straight week due to a calf injury suffered in the Steelers' Week 5 win against the Colts. Kaden Wetjen may see some extra reps in his place.

items.h: Ben Skowronek (calf) won't play Week 7
items.s: Ben Skowronek (calf) won't play in Week 7's matchup against the New Orleans Saints. The veteran wideout is going to miss another game due to the calf issue that he's recovering from. Rookie Germie Bernard was already expected to see a lot of work in this game, but this move clears his path to a large workload even more.

items.h: Ben Skowronek (calf) absent from practice Wednesday
items.s: Ben Skowronek (calf) was absent from practice on Wednesday. The veteran wideout wasn't able to practice on Wednesday thanks to a calf issue that he's still dealing with. He may very well be sidelined again in Week 7, which wouldn't have much of an impact for fantasy purposes.

items.h: Idle for Wednesday's practice
items.s: Skowronek (calf) did not practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports. Skowronek was unable to play against the Buccaneers in Week 6 due to a calf injury that he sustained during the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Colts. He'll have two more chances to log at least a limited practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris.

items.h: Already ruled out for Week 6
items.s: Head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that Skowronek (calf) will not play against the Buccaneers this Sunday, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports. Skowronek was diagnosed with a leg injury during the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts, which he picked up after a punt return in the first half. He was unable to return to the contest, and his calf issue will cost him at least one game, with his next chance to play being Week 7 against the Saints in Paris on Sunday, Oct. 25. Roman Wilson (finger) has also been ruled out for Week 6, so rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Smith are all in line for additional snaps on offense against Tampa Bay.

items.h: Ben Skowronek (calf) ruled out for Week 6
items.s: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek will not play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers. Skowronek left Sunday's game early against the Colts with a calf injury. He is week-to-week for now.

items.h: Ben Skowronek (calf) ruled out
items.s: The Steelers have ruled out WR Ben Skowronek (calf) for the remainder of the game with the Colts. Skowronek and Roman Wilson will not return for the Steelers in the second half. He did not receive a target prior to his injury.

items.h: Downgraded to out Sunday
items.s: Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Colts, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports. Skowronek exited the game with a leg injury after a punt return and was ruled questionable to return. After further evaluation, it has been determined the wide receiver will not return to Sunday's contest, leaving Brandon Smith as the No. 4 option.

items.h: Skowronek (leg) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
items.s: Skowronek was injured during a Steelers punt and is now in danger of missing the remainder of the Week 5 meeting with Indianapolis. The 29-year-old logged only eight offensive snaps in the Week 4 loss to the Browns, though his departure from the contest, even if it's brief, will be felt on special teams.

items.h: Skowronek hauled in his lone target for a 23-yard touchdown during Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.s: Skowronek ranked fifth among Steelers receivers by playing 11 of the team's 62 offensive snaps, but the 29-year-old was able to connect with quarterback Aaron Rodgers on a pass to the end zone during his limited time on the field. Despite coming up with a big play in the Week 3 win, Skowronek remains likely to see most of his field time on special teams moving forward.

items.h: Skowronek (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek was placed in concussion protocol at the end of August after the wide receiver suffered a head injury in the Steelers' 28-27 preseason loss to the Bills. The 29-year-old progressed through the entirety of the league's five-step protocol and was cleared by an independent neurologist before Wednesday's first official practice.

items.h: Skowronek suffered a concussion in Thursday's 28-27 preseason loss to the Bills, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. The wide receiver will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to ultimately be cleared for game action. If the 29-year-old cannot recover from the injury by the Steelers' Week 1 showdown with the Falcons, Kaden Wetjen projects to fill the No. 5 wide receiver role.

items.h: Skowronek secured four of six targets for 69 yards and a touchdown while appearing in all 17 regular-season games in 2025.
items.s: Skowronek had a 22-yard touchdown reception in the Steelers' Week 1 win over the Jets, but his production went downhill from there. He failed to garner multiple targets in any of his regular-season appearances, and he was forced to play mainly on special teams during his fifth professional campaign. The 2021 seventh-rounder will be an unrestricted free agent during the offseason, and it wouldn't be surprising to see him seek out other opportunities after being held under 70 receiving yards in each of his two seasons in Pittsburgh.

items.h: Skowronek (illness/hand) doesn't have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Similar to last week, Skowronek managed to log a full practice on the final day of the week to be cleared of any injury designation heading into gameday. This marks consecutive weeks that the wide receiver will play through a hand injury. The 28-year-old played just four offensive snaps last week with no targets, making his living on 65 percent of special teams snaps. This week will likely be no different for Skowronek, who sits behind DK Metcalf, Calvin Austin, Adam Thielen, and Marquez Valdes-Scantling on the wide receiver depth chart.

items.h: Skowronek (illness/hand) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
items.s: Skowronek dealt with the hand issue last week in practice, but the illness is new for the special-teams standout and wide receiver. Skowronek has posted a career-high 19 tackles (nine solo) in kick coverage for Pittsburgh.

items.h: Skowronek (hand) was not given an injury designation for Monday's clash against Miami.
items.s: Skowronek didn't practice Wednesday due to the hand issue, but he was able to finish the week with consecutive limited sessions. Those will be enough for the veteran wideout to take the field against the Dolphins on Monday Night Football. Skowronek has seen most of his work on special teams of late, as he has logged just 13 offensive snaps as opposed to 29 special-teams snaps over the past two weeks.

items.h: Skowronek (hand) was a limited participant in Friday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek was unable to practice Wednesday, so an upgrade in participation level is a good sign for the wide receiver's chances of playing in Monday night's game against the Dolphins. The 28-year-old will have one more opportunity to upgrade to a full participant and avoid an injury designation for Monday's game.

items.h: Skowronek (hand) did not participate in Thursday's practice, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek dealt with a shoulder injury during practice Week 14 but managed to suit up for the Steelers' win over Baltimore without any sort of designation. Now, however, the depth wideout's status appears uncertain due to a hand issue. Skowronek will have two more opportunities to get back on the practice field ahead of Monday's matchup against the Dolphins.

items.h: Skowronek (shoulder) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek upgraded to full practice participation Friday, just in time to dodge an injury designation ahead of Sunday's divisional tilt. The depth wide receiver has three receptions on five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown this season and has not missed a game.

items.h: Skowronek (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek missed some practice time last week with the same issue but ultimately didn't carry an injury designation into last Sunday's loss to the Bills, playing four offensive snaps. Skowronek has a 3-56-1 receiving line on five targets across 12 games this season.

items.h: Skowronek (shoulder) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Bills, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek logged a pair of DNPs Wednesday and Thursday before practicing fully Friday. The 28-year-old wide receiver has three catches for 56 yards and one touchdown on four targets across 11 appearances this season.

items.h: Skowronek (shoulder) didn't participate in Pittsburgh's practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek popped up on the injury report Wednesday, though it's unclear when he got hurt. The 28-year-old's availability in Thursday and Friday's practice sessions should provide more clarity on his status for Sunday's matchup versus the Bills.

items.h: Skowronek (neck) was a full practice participant Thursday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek was a limited participant Wednesday due to a neck issue, but he appears to be fine given his full participation one day later. The veteran wideout should be good to go for Sunday's Week 9 clash against the Colts, though he hasn't been a major part of Pittsburgh's offense with just two catches on three targets for 35 yards and a touchdown through seven contests.

items.h: Skowronek (neck) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek may have tweaked his neck during the Steelers' Week 8 loss to the Packers, when he played 39 snaps (11 on offense, 28 on special teams) while hauling in his lone target for a 13-yard catch. He has mostly served on special teams this season but would have a slightly expanded role on offense for as long as Scotty Miller is sidelined due to a broken finger. Skowronek's practice participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his chances of playing against the Colts on Sunday.

items.h: Skowronek secured his lone target for a 13-yard reception in Sunday's 35-25 loss to the Packers.
items.s: The reception was Skowronek's first since Week 1, when he had a 22-yard touchdown catch in a win over the Jets. He played just 11 of the Steelers' 63 snaps on offense Sunday and remains buried on the depth chart at receiver behind DK Metcalf, Calvin Austin and Roman Wilson.

items.h: Skowronek wasn't targeted during Sunday's 23-9 win over the Browns.
items.s: Although Calvin Austin (shoulder) was sidelined for Pittsburgh's Week 6 matchup Sunday, Skowronek played most of his snaps on special teams and wasn't involved in the passing game. Skowronek has been targeted just once over the Steelers' last four games, and he has minimal fantasy value, even if Austin is forced to miss more time.

items.h: Skowronek (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek was a full go Thursday after being limited by an illness Wednesday. He could see additional opportunities Sunday against the Browns if Calvin Austin (shoulder) is unable to play. Austin didn't practice in any capacity Wednesday or Thursday.

items.h: Skowronek (illness) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek opening Week 6 with a limited practice provides reason for optimism that he'll be able to gain clearance for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Browns. Prior to Pittsburgh's bye, Skowronek was targeted once during the team's win over the Vikings in Week 4, though he failed to log a reception. Through four regular-season appearances, the only catch Skowronek has logged is the 22-yard touchdown he recorded during the Steelers' win over the Jets in Week 1.

items.h: Skowronek failed to secure his lone target in Sunday's 24-21 win over the Vikings.
items.s: Skowronek caught a 22-yard touchdown during the Steelers' regular-season opener, but Sunday's overseas matchup was the first time he was targeted since then. Calvin Austin exited Sunday's game due to a shoulder injury, and it's not yet clear whether he'll be available following the Steelers' Week 5 bye. However, even if Austin misses time, Skowronek would likely be forced to compete for a role with Scotty Miller and Roman Wilson, and it's unlikely that any of them would have much fantasy upside behind DK Metcalf.

items.h: Skowronek wasn't targeted during Sunday's 31-17 loss to Seattle.
items.s: Skowronek reached the end zone during last week's regular-season opener, but he was unable to replicate his success in Week 2 as his snap count remained low. The 2021 seventh-rounder has played mainly on special teams early in the season, and he was on the field for just three offensive snaps Sunday. Although he made the most of his Week 1 target, it seems unlikely that he'll be a reliable fantasy option in 2025 as long as the rest of Pittsburgh's receivers stay healthy.

items.h: Skowronek secured his lone target for a 22-yard touchdown in Sunday's 34-32 win over the Jets.
items.s: Although Skowronek played just 10 offensive snaps during Sunday's regular-season opener, Aaron Rodgers found him late in the first quarter for the team's first touchdown of the year. It was encouraging to see Skowronek reach the end zone to open the regular season, but he'll likely have to compete with Roman Wilson and Scotty Miller for playing time behind DK Metcalf and Calvin Austin as the season progresses.

items.h: Skowronek (toe) played two snaps on special teams during Pittsburgh's 19-10 preseason win over the Panthers on Thursday.
items.s: Skowronek is back to full health after having sat out the Steelers' second preseason matchup due to a toe injury, but he didn't get any opportunities on offense during the exhibition finale. The 28-year-old wideout is competing to hang on to a reserve role as next week's cut-downs to a 53-man roster approach.

items.h: Steelers offensive coordinator Arthur Smith said Monday that Skowronek is dealing with a toe injury, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek didn't play in Saturday's preseason game after catching just one pass for three yards in Pittsburgh's exhibition opener. The veteran wideout is trying to hold on to one of the Steelers' final roster spots at the position behind DK Metcalf, Calvin Austin and Roman Wilson.

items.h: Skowronek secured his lone target for three yards during Saturday's 31-25 preseason win over the Jaguars.
items.s: Skowronek saw a limited role with the Steelers in 2024, securing all five of his targets for 69 yards across 10 regular-season appearances. He re-signed with the team during the offseason, but if he makes Pittsburgh's 53-man roster in 2025, he's unlikely to have a fantasy-relevant role.

items.h: The Steelers re-signed Skowronek on Thursday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Skowronek secured all five of his targets for 69 yards across 10 regular-season appearances with Pittsburgh in 2024. That marked the least productive season of Skowronek's career, but he dealt with injuries in the preseason and during the Steelers' regular-season finale. He'll work to remain healthy and carve out a greater role for 2025.

items.h: Skowronek appeared in 10 regular-season games for the Steelers in 2024, making five catches (on five targets) for 69 yards.
items.s: Skowronek's 10 appearances and five receptions were career lows. The former Ram joined Pittsburgh in mid-September after failing to make the Texans' 53-man roster out of training camp. An early season shoulder injury forced a six-game IR stint, while a hip injury late in the season was cause for another missed contest. Skowronek is set to be an unrestricted free agent.

items.h: Skowronek (hip) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek opened the Steelers' week of practice as a limited participant after missing the team's Christmas Day loss to the Chiefs. However, he upgraded to full participation Wednesday, suggesting he's since recovered from his hip injury. The 27-year-old is likely to serve as a depth piece in Pittsburgh's wide receiver room in the Week 18 matchup against the Bengals.

items.h: Skowronek (hip) was a limited participant in practice Tuesday, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek missed last Wednesday's Week 17 game against Kansas City due to a hip issue, but head coach Mike Tomlin indicated Monday that the fourth-year wideout is expected to be back for Saturday's matchup versus the Bengals. A limited practice session to open the week opens the door for that to happen, and the wideout's participation level Wednesday and Thursday should provide further clarity. If he does suit up Saturday, Skowronek will likely take on his usual depth role among the Steelers' wide-receiver corps.

items.h: Head coach Mike Tomlin relayed Monday that Skowronek and Joey Porter are both "scheduled to make it back" for Pittsburgh's regular-season finale against Cincinnati on Saturday, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek was unable to play against the Chiefs on Christmas day due to a hip injury that he suffered in Week 16 against the Ravens. He caught five passes on as many targets for 69 yards in the six games prior to his injury, and his return for Week 18 would bolster the Steelers' depth at wide receiver.

items.h: Skowronek (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Chiefs, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek suffered a hip injury during Pittsburgh's Week 16 loss to Baltimore this past Saturday. While he was able to return to that contest, the injury prevented him from participating in Monday's walkthrough and Tuesday's practice, and the 2021 seventh-round pick will be sidelined for Christmas Day. Skowronek's next opportunity to play will be in the Steelers' regular-season finale against the Bengals on Sunday, Jan. 5.

items.h: Head coach Mike Tomlin said Sunday that he's uncertain if Skowronek (hip) will be ready to play in the team's Week 17 game against the Chiefs on Wednesday, Missi Matthews of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek injured his hip in the first half of Saturday's 34-17 loss to the Ravens, though he was cleared to return to the contest. He finished with two receptions for 25 yards on two targets in the loss. Despite getting the green light to check back into Sunday's contest, Skowronek may be hurting now that the adrenaline has worn off. More clarity on his status for the Christmas Day game should come when the Steelers release injury reports Monday and Tuesday.

items.h: Skowronek (hip) returned to Saturday's game at Baltimore, Dale Lolley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek picked up a hip injury in the first half but rejoined the Steelers offense after halftime. He'll look to build upon the two catches (on two targets) for 25 yards that he had accrued before leaving the contest.

items.h: Skowronek is questionable to return to Saturday's game against the Steelers after suffering a hip injury.
items.s: Skowronek surprisingly had two critical first-down receptions on Pittsburgh's lone first-quarter scoring drive. Expect Scotty Miller and Calvin Austin to see more snaps in Skowronek's absence.

items.h: Skowronek is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Dale Lolley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek was placed on injured reserve with a shoulder injury prior to Week 3, and he'll be set for his first appearance since. He'll primarily play on special teams and is very unlikely to make any impact as a pass catcher.

items.h: The Steelers activated Skowronek (shoulder) off injured reserve Saturday, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster each of the first two weeks of the season, and he was then signed to the active roster in mid-September. However, the wideout was immediately placed on IR upon the signing. Skowronek was designated to return earlier this week, and with his activation, he could return to the field Sunday against Washington. If he is active for the contest, Skowronek probably won't see much work on offense given that Pittsburgh's wideout corps is largely healthy and that he didn't see a target during either of the two games he has been active…

items.h: Skowronek (shoulder) participated at practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek has been on Pittsburgh's injured reserve list since he was signed due to a shoulder issue, but it now appears he could be approaching a return to the field. The Steelers have 21 days to activate him to their active roster before they'd have to keep him on IR for the rest of the season.

items.h: Skowronek (shoulder) was signed to the Steelers' 53-man roster Tuesday, then placed on injured reserve Wednesday.
items.s: Skowronek was elevated from the practice squad for each of Pittsburgh's first two games but hasn't had much of a role in the offense. His move to injured reserve will keep him sidelined for at least the next four weeks but, presumably, he'll be a part of the 53-man roster once he's healthy after his signing to the active roster Wednesday.

items.h: Skowronek is dealing with shoulder soreness Tuesday, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
items.s: Skowronek has been elevated from the Steelers' practice squad each of the first two weeks of the season. However, that has mostly led to a special teams role, as he's only seen six snaps on offense. This injury could impact his role this Sunday against the Chargers and keep him on the practice squad, as Calvin Austin (undisclosed) and Roman Wilson (ankle) deal with injuries as well. Pittsburgh currently has Quez Watkins, Brandon Johnson and Shaquan Davis as options at receiver on their practice squad, too.

items.h: Skowronek reverted to the Steelers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.s: Skowronek was elevated to the active roster for the second consecutive week to kick off the season. The depth receiver saw the field for six of 66 offensive snaps, as well as 12 on special teams. Skowronek did not draw any targets, however, but he was credited with one tackle.

items.h: The Steelers elevated Skowronek from their practice squad Saturday ahead of the team's Week 2 matchup versus Denver.
items.s: Skowronek was also elevated ahead of Week 1 and played 10 snaps -- all on special teams -- against Atlanta. He'll likely have a similar role this Sunday while serving as wideout depth with rookie receiver Roman Wilson questionable to suit up due to an ankle injury.

items.h: Skowronek reverted to Pittsburgh's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.s: Skowronek played all ten of his snaps on special teams during the Steelers' win at Atlanta in Week 1. It looks like the Steelers aspire to be a run-heavy offense in 2024 as long as game script allows, so there probably won't be many weeks where Pittsburgh pass catchers not named George Pickens draw enough target volume for fantasy consideration in most leagues.

items.h: The Steelers elevated Skowronek to the active roster Saturday, Brian Batko of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.
items.s: Skowronek will be called up for the Steelers' regular-season opener against the Falcons on Sunday due to rookie wideout Roman Wilson (ankle) being ruled out. With the Rams in 2023, Skowronek registered eight catches (on 12 targets) for 66 yards and one touchdown across 17 regular-season games. If he sees the field, the 2021 seventh-round pick will contribute on special teams while providing depth at wide receiver.

items.h: Skowronek signed to Pittsburgh's practice squad Friday, Teresa Varley of the teams official site reports.
items.s: Skowronek spent training camp with the Texans and caught four of eight targets for 32 yards over three preseason contests. He was unable to make Houston's 53-man roster, however, and will now look to make his way back to NFL action via Pittsburgh's practice squad. Skowronek spent his first three professional campaigns with the Rams, compiling 58 receptions on 93 targets for 575 yards and one touchdown while rushing three times for 26 yards and another score over 45 regular-season games.
